description:
From the fz-kdt.107 cold review's Q4 dig, CORRECTED by its addendum
(2026-09-01): the review first read 00277's dbg[empty_list()] vs
dbg[list(int)] pair as a hole in fz-kdt.106's absorption -- WRONG.
Types::row_dominates has exactly two call sites, both inside
insert_row (semantic.rs:~917,922): the rule is scoped to ONE activation
key's correlated-row antichain BY CONSTRUCTION and never compares two
keys. That pair is a different question entirely (cross-key
specialization subsumption -- see its own ticket).

WHAT THIS TICKET ACTUALLY OWNS: within one key, two rows differing only
in a CAPTURED CLOSURE position (00277's FIFO
Range.reduce/5[...{:cont,empty_list()}...] pair: Enum.reverse/1#lambda
vs /2#lambda captures) are not absorbed although the payload column is
dominated -- lit_arrow_shapes containment fails across distinct fn_ids.
NOTE: this is a DELIBERATE guard, documented in row_column_dominates as
stopping a template row from absorbing its ground sibling -- not an
oversight. The question is whether callable columns should instead be
compared through their runtime-observable erasure (fun_top), the same
judgement fz-kdt.118 is making for the dispatch drop rule. SEQUENCE
BEHIND fz-kdt.118: if 118's observable-surface judgement survives its
refuter (its soundness obligation is the same one), evaluate the
analogous relaxation here with the same discipline -- and remember the
relation's antisymmetry/termination are EMPIRICAL (documented as "a
fact about today's inputs, not a theorem"), so any relaxation re-runs
the oscillation attack.
title: Closure positions shield dominance: should the kdt.106 absorption compare callable columns through their runtime-observable erasure?
